title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-node-pools-iam-networking-migration
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: unify the Terraform state layout used by Private deployments and introduce a first-class GPU node-pools module plus consolidated IAM and networking primitives to simplify upgrades and reduce drift across customer installations. This change is targeted at Private installer and Terraform consumers (on-prem/VPC) and follows the state layout proposal in ENG-4821. Summary of changes: 1) Add a new modules/gpu_node_pools module that encapsulates node pool creation, node taints/labels, autoscaler config, and GKE/AKS/eks-agnostic variable mappings. 2) Rework the state layout to split 'cluster' and 'platform' statefiles to enable per-cluster ownership in multi-cluster private installs and reduce locking contention. 3) Consolidate IAM role modules into modules/iam_common with clearer least-privilege defaults and predictable role naming to avoid drift. 4) Networking refactor: expose modular subnetwork creation and peering helpers so private deployments can adopt existing customer VPC layouts without hacks. 5) Migration helpers and scripts: terraform state mv plan generator plus a small helper script (scripts/state-migration.sh) to automate state moves in a predictable sequence. Compatibility and rollout: default variables preserve previous behavior; an opt-in variable private_state_layout = "unified-v2" flips to the new layout. The migration script is idempotent and includes a dry-run mode. Rollback plan: keep previous layout artifacts intact until migration completes; the script provides a revert sequence; we recommend performing migration during a maintenance window and validating control-plane resources before worker reconfiguration. Testing and validation: added end-to-end tests in perf-canary to validate node pool scaling, KV cache connectivity, and IAM binding coverage. Updated examples in redwood-private-installer to show the new module usage. Documentation: updated README, UPGRADE.md and added a migration checklist under docs/migration.md. Followups: introduce automated state migration PR job in CI and add a telemetry tag to track migrations. Checklist: - [x] module implementation - [x] state layout proposal implemented - [x] migration scripts + dry-run - [x] integration tests - [x] docs and examples updated - [x] reviewer approvals
commits: refactor: split state layout into cluster/platform statefiles
chore(iam): consolidate iam roles into modules/iam_common
test: add e2e migration validation in perf-canary
review_comments: Liam Chen: Small nit on variable naming in gpu_node_pools/variables.tf (use 'node_pool' prefix for consistency).
Aisha Khan (author): Thanks, updated names and added a deprecation note for the old variables in variables.tf to aid migration.
Priya Rao: Confirmed IAM role bindings are constrained to service account principals used by the runtime; please add a short note about cross-account assumptions.
Aisha Khan (author): Added note and explicit variable for external_principals with sane defaults.
Diego Martinez: CI showed a transient e2e failure on first run (GKE quota). Re-ran and all checks passed. Please ensure migration script handles partial state errors gracefully.
Aisha Khan (author): Migration script now supports --retry and logs a suggested manual rollback sequence on failure.
release_notes: - Introduce modules/gpu_node_pools for GPU worker management and autoscaling. - Unify private deployment Terraform state layout (v2) with migration tooling and dry-run support. - Consolidate IAM roles into modules/iam_common with least-privilege defaults. - Networking helpers for subnet and peering to support flexible customer VPCs. - Migration script and migration checklist added to docs/UPGRADE.md.
notes: Migrated several internal customers without downtime during staged rollout. Recommend bumping the private-installer chart version when releasing this change.
